root_draft.text: The Pyrelands are a grass savanna that has burned for millennia and is burning still. Almost all the ground is deep ash, quite fertile wherever water reaches it, carpeted thick in ember grass that burns black and is largely green again within about a week, while free-flying ash blows across it like snow. A line of grass fire walks the map and never fully goes out. Behind it the fire pays: scorch-fruit grows only from freshly burned ground and must be picked before it rots, and fresh burns grow crops faster for a few days, and black rain washes the bonus away early. The animals are the fire's own cast: a fire-hawk carries a burning twig ahead of the blaze to start a new fire, ullai herds graze where it burned two days ago, the ashwallow dives underground as the front reaches it and comes through unharmed, and the giant furnace-beast warms anyone standing near it and heats a room it shelters in. The sky brings ash fall, cinderfall and black rain, and never ordinary rain. Ruins stand blackened. The biome is whole on its own, with no other mod's plants or animals, and (built, not yet in your words) a sprayed firebreak line and a firefoam sprayer let a colony defend its fields. Judged first: a fresh map in ordinary play where the burn line is visibly walking across deep ash with a scorched trail behind it, and a few days later the grass behind it is greening and scorch-fruit stands in the scar.
